title: Find the Integer Added to Array I
statement:
The arrays `nums1` and `nums2` have the same length. Some integer `x` (positive, negative or zero) was added to every element of `nums1`, and afterwards `nums1` holds exactly the values of `nums2` with the same counts, though possibly in a different order.

Return `x`. The input guarantees that such an `x` exists.
constraints: Some integer x turns nums1 into nums2 (as a multiset) when added to every element
notes:
## Intuition

One could try every `x` from -1000 to 1000 and compare sorted arrays, but there is a shortcut. Adding the same `x` to every value shifts the whole array without changing its order, so the smallest value of `nums1` must become the smallest value of `nums2`. Hence `x = min(nums2) - min(nums1)`.

## Approach

1. Start `smallest1` and `smallest2` at the first element of each array.
2. Scan the remaining positions, keeping the minimum of each array (the two arrays have the same length, so one loop serves both).
3. Return `smallest2 - smallest1`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums1 = [2, 6, 4]`, `nums2 = [9, 7, 5]`. Start with `smallest1 = 2`, `smallest2 = 9`.

- `i = 1`: `smallest1 = min(2, 6) = 2`, `smallest2 = min(9, 7) = 7`.
- `i = 2`: `smallest1 = min(2, 4) = 2`, `smallest2 = min(7, 5) = 5`.

The answer is `5 - 2 = 3`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n), one pass over both arrays.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- Do not subtract `nums2[i] - nums1[i]` position by position: the arrays only match as multisets, so the order may differ.
- `x` can be negative; return the signed difference, not its absolute value.
- The maximum works just as well; mixing a minimum of one array with a maximum of the other does not.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `smallest1` | smallest value of `nums1` seen so far |
| `smallest2` | smallest value of `nums2` seen so far |
| `i` | current position in both arrays |

narration.2: Begin with the first value of nums1 as its smallest so far.
narration.4: Walk through the remaining positions of both arrays together.
narration.5: Keep the smaller of the current minimum and nums1[i].
narration.6: Keep the smaller of the current minimum and nums2[i].
narration.8: Shifting every value by x shifts the minimum by x, so the difference of minimums is x.
